newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on short-covering, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,150 yuan ($379) per tonne, rising 20 yuan. It opened at 3,130 and hit a low of 3,100.
March rose 30 to 3,170, May 11 to 3,149, July 63 to 3,238, September fell 84 to 3,298 and November 19 to 3,360.
Combined volume rose to 53,500 tonnes from 47,600.
Traders said short-covering dominated today's trading but the short-term market trend remained unclear.
"Many investors want to liquidate their positions with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday," one trader said.
"But the short-term market trend is not clear given the lack of market-moving news," he added.
Traders expect soybeans to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
